text:
sam: Hey team, new hire here — first week working on the runtime. Trying to build locally on WSL2 (Win11) and hitting a few issues: large C++ link step dies with `g++: internal compiler error: Killed (program cc1plus)` and linker later complains `cannot find -lcudart`. Followed README for dev setup. Any pointers?

anya: welcome! cc1plus killed is usually OOM in WSL. Check WSL memory config. Run `wsl -l -v` and drop a .wslconfig in your Windows user home to bump memory/swap or reduce parallelism with `make -j2`.

sam: `wsl -l -v` shows Ubuntu-22.04, default settings. I tried `make -j2` and it got further but still `cannot find -lcudart`. I installed CUDA toolkit on Windows, but not sure if WSL sees it.

kevin: for CUDA-on-WSL you need both the Windows NVIDIA driver with WSL support and the Linux toolkit installed inside WSL. Inside WSL run `nvidia-smi` to confirm driver visible. Also ensure `/usr/local/cuda` exists (symlink to the toolkit dir) and that `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` is known to the linker (`/etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf` + `sudo ldconfig`).

sam: `nvidia-smi` returns GPU info. There is `/usr/local/cuda-12.2` but no `/usr/local/cuda`.

anya: create the symlink: `sudo ln -s /usr/local/cuda-12.2 /usr/local/cuda` then `sudo ldconfig`. Also export `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` before building so auto-detect picks it up. Our CI uses `--with-cuda=/usr/local/cuda-12.2` to be explicit.

sam: created symlink and set `CUDA_HOME`, ran `make` again — now hits `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterFatBinary` during link.

kevin: that usually means the cuda runtime library wasn't linked in. Make sure `-lcudart` is present in link flags or `CUDA_LIBS=-L/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -lcudart` is set. Also avoid `-Wl,--as-needed` removing libcudart; we use `-Wl,--no-as-needed -lcudart` in the Makefile. If the build system didn't detect CUDA, the flags can be missing.

sam: exporting `CUDA_HOME` fixed it and build completed. Two onboarding suggestions if that's ok: add a short WSL checklist to onboarding (increase memory via .wslconfig, symlink tip, set CUDA_HOME, run ldconfig), and mention to avoid full-parallel builds on low-memory dev VMs. Happy to draft a PR.

anya: please do — PR into `docs/onboarding-devbox.md` and ping me. infra-bot: https://intra.redwood/dev-onboard/wsl-cuda contains existing notes, link there in the PR.

sam: will draft now, thanks all :)
